lessons.title: Thông báo của tòa nhà
lessons.context: Bạn đọc một thông báo dán ở sảnh chung cư.
meta: Chủ đề: Cắt nước ngày thứ Tư
paragraphs: Dear residents,
Please note that the water will be turned off on Wednesday, 14 May, from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. because we need to repair a pipe on the roof.
We suggest you store some water in advance for cooking and drinking. The lifts will work as usual.
If you have any questions, please call the office on 555 0142. Thank you for your understanding.

lessons.title: Đánh giá một quán ăn
lessons.context: Bạn đọc một bài đánh giá ngắn trên mạng về một quán ăn mới.
paragraphs: We went to Green Garden last Saturday with my parents. It is a small vegetarian restaurant near the park.
The food was fresh and cheap. I had the mushroom soup, and my father loved the tofu curry. The only problem was the waiting time: we waited about thirty minutes for our food.
The staff were very friendly and the restaurant was clean. I will definitely go again, but I will book a table first.

unit.title: Chặng 1 · Đọc bài ngắn và nắm ý chính

lessons.title: Làm việc từ xa: lợi và hại
lessons.context: Bạn đọc một bài viết ngắn về làm việc tại nhà.
paragraphs: More and more people now work from home at least two days a week. For many, the biggest advantage is saving time: there is no long journey to the office, so they have more time for family and exercise.
However, working at home is not always easy. Some people find it hard to separate work from free time, and they end up answering emails late at night. Others miss talking to colleagues face to face.
Experts suggest setting clear working hours and using a separate room, if possible. A short walk before and after work can also help your brain to switch on and off.

What problem do some people have?
What do experts suggest?

lessons.title: Cách học nói tiếng Anh hằng ngày
lessons.context: Bạn đọc một bài chia sẻ kinh nghiệm luyện nói tiếng Anh.
meta: Tác giả: Một người học tiếng Anh
paragraphs: When I started learning English, I understood a lot but I could hardly speak. I was afraid of making mistakes, so I stayed silent in class.

Everything changed when I began to talk to myself for ten minutes every evening. I described my day, what I ate and what I planned for tomorrow. At first it felt strange, but after a month I noticed that I was finding words much faster.
I also record myself once a week and listen again. It is not pleasant to hear your own mistakes, but it is the quickest way to improve.

What did the writer do every evening?
options: Talked to himself for ten minutes

questions.question: What is the benefit of recording yourself?
options: It is the quickest way to improve

lessons.title: Hướng dẫn thăm một thành phố nhỏ
lessons.context: Bạn đọc một đoạn giới thiệu du lịch.
paragraphs: Hoi An is a small town on the central coast of Vietnam, famous for its old buildings and lanterns. Most visitors spend two or three days there.
The best time to visit is between February and April, when the weather is warm and dry. In autumn, heavy rain can cause floods, so many hotels offer lower prices.
You can rent a bicycle for a dollar a day and ride to the beach, which is only four kilometres from the centre. Do not forget to try the local noodles, which are cheap and delicious.

When is the best time to visit?
Why are hotels cheaper in autumn?
options: Fewer tourists want rain and floods

questions.question: The beach is far from the town centre.

unit.title: Chặng 1 · Đọc hiểu theo dạng IELTS

lessons.title: Xe đạp công cộng trong thành phố
lessons.context: Bạn đọc một bài báo ngắn, dạng bài đọc phần 1 của IELTS.
meta: Nguồn: Bài báo về giao thông đô thị
paragraphs: Over the past decade, bicycle-sharing schemes have spread to more than a thousand cities worldwide. Supporters claim that they reduce traffic and pollution, while also encouraging people to exercise.
Critics, however, point out that the bikes are often left on pavements, which causes problems for pedestrians. In several cities, thousands of damaged bikes have ended up in landfills.

A recent study in Paris found that the schemes mainly replaced walking and public transport rather than car journeys. This suggests that the environmental benefits may be smaller than originally believed.
Despite this, many city councils remain optimistic and are investing in protected cycle lanes, hoping that safer roads will persuade more drivers to switch.

What do critics complain about?
What did the Paris study find?

lessons.title: Thói quen ngủ của người trẻ
lessons.context: Bạn đọc một bài nghiên cứu ngắn và tìm ý chính từng đoạn.
paragraphs: Sleep specialists have long warned that teenagers need between eight and ten hours of sleep a night, yet surveys suggest that fewer than a third actually achieve this.
One major cause is the use of screens late in the evening. The blue light they emit can delay the release of melatonin, the hormone that makes us feel sleepy.
Some schools have responded by starting lessons an hour later. In one trial, students at these schools not only slept longer but also reported feeling less anxious and performed better in exams.
Nevertheless, critics argue that later start times simply push the problem to the evening, when students go to bed even later.

options: They delay the release of melatonin

options: Students slept longer and performed better

questions.question: All experts agree that later school start times solve the problem.

lessons.title: Học ngôn ngữ ở người trưởng thành
lessons.context: Bạn đọc một bài phân tích và tìm quan điểm của tác giả.
paragraphs: It is commonly assumed that children learn languages more easily than adults. While young learners often develop a more natural accent, research indicates that adults can in fact progress faster in the early stages, thanks to their ability to analyse grammar and use learning strategies.
The key difference lies in consistency. Children are usually surrounded by the language for many hours a day, whereas most adults can only dedicate a short time to study.

Consequently, the most effective approach for adults is not longer study sessions, but frequent short ones. Fifteen minutes of speaking practice every day, for example, tends to produce better results than a three-hour session once a week.

questions.question: What do adults often do better than children at first?
options: Progress faster in the early stages

What does the writer recommend for adults?
